title: Track 3 verification protocol
core_rule: PASS is only valid for the named claim when its evidence gates are satisfied. No evidence -> UNKNOWN. An unrun test -> NOT_TESTED. No status is inferred from another status.

evidence_requirements: source URL or stable record locator

FAIL.meaning: Claim-specific evidence explicitly contradicts the claim.

UNKNOWN.meaning: Test/search was attempted but evidence is insufficient for PASS or FAIL.

UNASSESSED.meaning: No verifier has assigned a result.

claims.UNIVERSE_ENTRY: Facility/request is in the declared Track 3 research population.
claims.AI_COMPUTE_PUBLISHER_CHECK: Epoch explicitly records AI-data-center compute evidence; publisher/derived check only.
claims.SITE_IDENTITY: Facility has stable identity and site locator.
claims.POWER_OBSERVATION: Site-specific electricity observation exists with source, time/period and units.
claims.PHYSICAL_REMOTE_SENSING: Site-level optical/TIR/SAR observation is acquired and traceable.
claims.INDEPENDENT_CORROBORATION: Material claim is supported by distinct retained sources.
claims.END_TO_END_TRACK3: Physical, electrical, compute and independent-verifier chain is sufficient for the exact claim.
claims.ARTIFACT_ATTESTATION: Verification bundle has a valid cryptographic attestation.

GRID_CONNECTION: site-specific queue/service/interconnection identifier or equivalent site-specific primary utility record

absence_testing_rule: A no-match/no-found statement must point to a retained search record naming the source/database, URL/locator, capture date, search scope and result. Missing rows or fields are not absence evidence.
versioning_rule: Every result carries protocol_version, generation timestamp and source_snapshot_commit. Historical artifacts are retained by Git.
independent_verifier: The repository has a separate read-only verifier workflow and a standalone verify_track3.py procedure. This is operational separation, not a claim of organizational independence; a third party can run the same verifier against an immutable commit.
signed_audit: The verification workflow produces a verification bundle and uses GitHub Artifact Attestations (Sigstore-backed) to create a cryptographic provenance/integrity claim for that bundle.
dispute_correction: Corrections use append-only GitHub issues/events with facility/evidence IDs, proposed change, source and rationale; old snapshots are retained.
